column1: # cardinality.tsv — sections that STATE how many cases they have, and the number they state.
# crisp-tallying-chapters §5: "Combinatorial chapters declare their cardinality from the spec.
# §5.1.2 states 19 widening conversions; if §5.1.2 claims COVERED the gate asks *by how many
# cases* and compares against 19. A missing generator is a failing count, not a silent zero.
# This is the check that makes stitching impossible to skip."
# The problem it solves is real and was live when this file was written: the generator's
# per-type cap had kept 17 of §5.1.2's 19 conversions, and the ledger said COVERED — because a
# `// JLS 5.1.2` marker is produced identically by one surviving case and by all nineteen.
# A row here is a QUOTE, not a judgement. Only sections whose own text names a count belong;
# "this section feels combinatorial" is not a cardinality. The sentence is carried so the
# number can be checked against the spec without opening the PDF, and so a wrong number is a
# visible disagreement rather than an unexplained constant.
